correctness.rationale: After conditioning on Pi(i)=i, any descent comparison not incident to i remains symmetric. For incident comparisons, exact counts among the n-1 remaining values give probabilities (j-1)/(n-1) and (n-j-1)/(n-1). These yield the displayed local covariance matrix. Row and column summation gives the ordinary formulas, and conditioning at positions 1 or n shows the wrap indicator contributes +1/(2n), cancelling the endpoint terms exactly.

originality.rationale: Classical literature gives strong joint enumeration of descent classes with the total number of fixed points, and separate probability theory for the fixed-point random set. The inspected sources do not retain the fixed-point position and therefore do not state the local cross-covariance matrix or its endpoint/cyclic cancellation. The global covariance alone is not presented as the originality claim.

value.rationale: Fixed points and descents are canonical local permutation statistics. The position-resolved covariance matrix reveals a non-obvious cancellation geometry: bulk fixed points have zero net covariance with total descents, while the two boundary coordinates alone produce the global negative covariance. Cyclic closure cancels those remaining terms coordinatewise, giving a clean structural explanation rather than only an isolated mixed moment.
